issue: Published legal and shipping placeholders undermine informed enquiries and purchases
urls: All nine /termek/ pages; homepage and /kapcsolat/ forms
evidence: The privacy, terms and shipping pages say they are being uploaded. All nine product HTML documents contain a [HIÁNYZIK: ...] shipping note; it was also displayed by opening the priced product's shipping tab. The enquiry form requires acceptance of the incomplete terms and privacy notice.
why: Visitors cannot review the information they are asked to accept or determine delivery costs and timing. This is an immediate trust and operational-readiness risk; legal compliance requires qualified review.
solution: Publish company-approved privacy, terms, delivery/payment and returns information; remove internal editorial notes from all product tabs. Review the enquiry checkbox's legal basis and wording with counsel. Gate transactional promotion until purchase policies and fulfilment are approved.
acceptance: All linked policies contain approved, dated text; no public HIÁNYZIK or feltöltés alatt placeholders; enquiry consent wording matches the actual processing.

issue: Eight of nine products lack a clear commercial next step
evidence: Only the 22 kW / 7.5 m product displays 99 999 Ft and an add-to-cart control. The other eight have empty price elements; cards say Tovább olvasom. The sampled unpriced 11 kW / 5 m page has an English Contact us now link in a separate installation panel.
why: Buyers cannot tell whether a product is available, quotation-only, temporarily unavailable or unfinished. The price is observed, not independently validated as correct.
solution: Choose purchase or quote mode per product. Show approved price, stock/lead-time and VAT/installation scope for purchasable products. For quote mode use Ár és telepítési ajánlat kérése beside the product title and preserve model/variant in the enquiry.
acceptance: Every product has one unambiguous primary action and availability state; business owner signs off prices; quote requests carry product context.

issue: Navigation prominently exposes seven empty product categories
evidence: The shop navigation shows zero products in seven categories and nine in Autótöltők. The Légkezelők page explains that upload is in progress, shows an empty result and recommends unrelated EV chargers.
why: The site promises a broad HVAC store but exposes an EV-charger-only catalogue. Empty, indexable pages offer little search or purchase value.
solution: Turn quote-led categories into useful specification/enquiry landing pages, clearly distinguish them from buy-online ranges, and remove irrelevant popular-product widgets. If a category is genuinely unfinished, hide it from purchase navigation and temporarily noindex it rather than presenting a dead end.
acceptance: Each promoted category offers useful products or a focused specification/quote path; no unexplained zero-result routes remain.

issue: Shared color tokens make important text difficult to read
urls: Sampled product page; related dark hero templates
evidence: axe measured service-hero checklist text at 1.82:1 (#3a4a57 on #0f1f2f), active service navigation at 2.71:1, contact links at 3.49:1 and some homepage CTA text at 4.44:1. Related hero checklist text is visibly dark in the solutions/about/reference screenshots.
why: Users with low vision and people viewing a phone in glare may miss the very proof points and actions intended to persuade them. Normal text requires 4.5:1 for WCAG AA.
solution: Introduce semantic light-on-dark and dark-on-light text tokens; do not inherit body color inside dark heroes. Adjust green text/button combinations, add non-color active/link cues and retest default, hover, focus and disabled states across templates.
acceptance: All normal text in audited templates reaches 4.5:1, large text 3:1; regressions checked by automated and visual tests.

issue: Homepage discovery controls imply destinations they do not reach
evidence: Four Tudjon meg többet links point back to the homepage. Industry cards reveal a Megoldások → span rather than an anchor; keyboard Enter flips the card, and clicking the span did not navigate. All ten service cards point to the same services overview without a fragment.
why: Users repeat work, lose context and may interpret the interface as broken. Search engines receive no distinct destination from pseudo-links.
solution: Link the four benefit CTAs to relevant service/about/proof sections. Replace industry pseudo-links with actual anchors to matching industry sections/pages. Add stable service anchors immediately; use dedicated detail URLs when substantive pages are ready.
acceptance: Every apparent link reaches a relevant destination using mouse, touch and keyboard; each service/industry card preserves context.

issue: Large, eagerly requested background images dominate homepage payload
evidence: A desktop resource sample recorded 2,624,647 encoded body bytes for the restaurant PNG and 645,151 for the hero JPG. Known document-plus-resource transfer was 5,612,237 bytes before a full-page scroll; opaque third-party sizes are excluded.
why: Fast desktop rendering does not remove mobile data and slower-network costs. Offscreen industry imagery competes for bandwidth with the initial experience.
solution: Create appropriately sized WebP/AVIF variants, preserve visual quality, use responsive picture/img markup for meaningful imagery and load below-fold backgrounds on demand. Keep the actual LCP image eager; avoid indiscriminately lazy-loading the hero.
acceptance: Restaurant image is right-sized and modern-format; offscreen cards no longer download unnecessarily at initial load; cold mobile lab tests show a smaller measured payload without image or layout regressions.

issue: Ten services and six sectors lack deep, intent-specific landing paths
evidence: Services are short sections within one overview; industry content also lives on a single overview. The 29-page crawl and sitemap review found no separate commercial detail pages for maintenance, air-handler renovation or custom filter manufacture.
why: A high-intent visitor cannot land directly on a complete explanation of one need. The existing breadth is diluted rather than organized into useful search destinations.
solution: Retain the two hubs. Build original detail pages first for légkezelő karbantartás, légkezelő felújítás/forgódob-csere and egyedi légtechnikai szűrőgyártás; connect them to sector examples, relevant products and a contextual enquiry. Add further pages only when genuine unique detail is available.
acceptance: Each new page answers scope, fit, process, proof and next-step questions and is linked from its hub; no near-duplicate doorway pages.

issue: Reference content describes project types rather than evidenced case studies
evidence: References use labels such as Ipari üzem and Szálloda without client/project identity, dates, specifications or demonstrated outcomes. Filter-product images lead the reference page. The About page asserts a CompanyWall AA+ rating and top 1.1% standing without a verification link in the inspected main content.
why: A procurement buyer needs evidence of comparable delivery, not only an assertion of capability. Generic imagery weakens the connection between claim and proof.
solution: Publish permission-cleared case studies with site/sector, date, problem, scope, real project photographs and documented results. Where clients are confidential, say so and include verifiable technical specifics. Link to current certification/rating evidence and identify responsible experts.
acceptance: Three representative case studies have approved evidence; numerical claims and ratings have a source/date; no fabricated testimonials or savings.

issue: The enquiry form asks for more effort than necessary
evidence: The form includes first/last name, email, telephone, company, subject, enquiry type and message plus policy acceptance. Telephone is marked aria-required and is type=text with no inputmode or autocomplete; email and telephone are both required by the plugin's ARIA markers. Labels are correctly associated.
why: Required telephone plus email, a separate subject and unassisted technical description add friction, especially on phones. This is a design concern, not a measured abandonment rate.
solution: Keep clear labels; make phone optional unless callback is chosen; consider a single full-name field and remove redundant subject. Use type=tel, autocomplete tokens and concise prompts for building/location/equipment. Preserve incoming service/product context. Explain what happens next using an approved response expectation.
acceptance: Mobile autofill and keyboard types work; only necessary inputs are mandatory; empty/invalid/error/success states and email delivery pass an authorized staging test.

issue: Product and category search snippets are unfinished
evidence: All 17 product/category pages lack meta descriptions. Category titles retain the English Archives suffix. The shop title is only Webshop - NEXTRO Kft. Main service-page metadata is present and distinct.
why: Search snippets and shared links communicate less clearly than the underlying product data allows. Meta descriptions influence presentation, not guaranteed ranking or click-through gains.
solution: Write differentiated Hungarian descriptions for commercial pages and replace archive defaults with customer-facing category titles. Include model/power/cable variants on products and use a specific shop title. Resolve real catalogue availability before promising online purchase.
acceptance: All intended commercial landing pages have relevant distinct titles and descriptions; previews are reviewed by pixel width, not only character count.

issue: Category headings and section hierarchy are inconsistent
urls: Six category URLs listed in the technical inventory
evidence: Six of 29 crawled pages have no H1: Alkatrészek, Automatika, Fűtőegységek, Légfüggönyök, Légkezelők and Szűrők. Párásítók does have an H1. The solutions page puts Hotel/Wellness at H2 but peer sectors at H3. Contact jumps from H1 to H3.
why: Visual peers do not form predictable document sections for scanning and assistive navigation. Missing H1s reduce topic clarity; they are not proof of a ranking penalty.
solution: Render one descriptive H1 on category templates, make peer sectors the same heading level and use H2 section labels with H3 subtopics. Do not select heading tags to achieve a font size.
acceptance: Category pages have a meaningful H1 and all audited templates have a logical outline independent of visual styling.

issue: The sitemap includes noindex and redirecting utility routes
evidence: The page sitemap includes cart, checkout and account routes. Cart and account return noindex, follow; an empty-session checkout request redirects 302 to cart. The shop URL occurs in both page and product sitemaps.
why: The sitemap sends mixed discovery/indexing signals and contains routes that are not organic landing pages. The duplicate shop entry is redundant, not a duplicate-content penalty.
solution: Exclude utility/noindex routes from the sitemap and deduplicate shop inclusion. Keep cart/account noindex and allow crawlers to see that directive. Submit the cleaned sitemap in Search Console once access is available.
acceptance: Every sitemap page entry resolves directly to an intended indexable canonical 200 URL; cart, checkout and account are absent.

issue: Product presentation makes model comparison unnecessarily difficult
evidence: Nine power/cable variants are presented as separate long-title cards with different lifestyle crops; the priced product uses a wide landscape image. Descriptions contain a dense shared specification paragraph and optional comparison controls, but decision-critical differences are not in a concise visible grid.
why: Users must read repetitive names to compare power, phases and cable options and cannot easily assess included hardware versus installation imagery.
solution: Use consistent product packshots and aspect ratios, a power/phase/cable comparison table and a labelled installation/gallery section. Keep imagery accurate to the offered SKU. Consider a single variant selector only after assessing URL demand and migration implications.
acceptance: Variant differences and included items are visible without opening every product; any URL consolidation has an explicit redirect/canonical plan.

issue: Mobile contact access and menu ergonomics can be improved
evidence: At 390 px the menu button's measured box is 18 × 18 px. The desktop phone strip is hidden; homepage phone links appear far down the long page. The menu opens successfully and major tested pages fit the viewport.
why: A small target is harder to hit; an urgent maintenance visitor has no immediate call action in the mobile header. This is an ergonomic finding, not a proven WCAG target-size violation because spacing exceptions may apply.
solution: Give menu/close controls a 44 × 44 px design target with visible focus; add a labelled call action and/or compact quote/call bar after consent. Respect safe areas and avoid obscuring the form or cookie controls. Test opened-menu keyboard focus, Escape and return focus across devices.
acceptance: Menu and close controls have comfortable touch areas; phone/quote access is immediate on mobile; no overlay collision at 320–430 px.

issue: Consent and third-party integration need a documented verification pass
evidence: Browser resource logs include MailerLite and Barion resources. The cookie interface offers accept, reject and settings, but some preference text in the raw page is English. Network presence alone does not establish tracking purpose, payload, consent compliance or unlawful processing.
why: The incomplete privacy notice and third-party integrations make it important to verify what loads, stores or transmits data under each consent choice rather than assume the banner controls everything.
solution: In a clean-browser matrix, compare no choice/reject/granular/accept/revoke states. Classify each integration and its legal basis, gate non-essential behavior as appropriate and publish matching disclosures. Translate residual English preference/help text and verify newsletter confirmation handling.
acceptance: A retained request/storage audit maps each integration to purpose and consent behavior; policy and banner agree. This is a verification task, not a finding of a legal violation.

issue: Structured data is basic and uneven across the catalogue
evidence: Homepage JSON-LD includes WebPage, WebSite, Organization, ImageObject and breadcrumbs. Organization contains name/URL/logo but not address, telephone or sameAs. Only the priced product has Product/Offer JSON-LD; its price is 99999 HUF and availability is InStock.
why: The entity graph omits useful verified business details; quote-only items are not represented consistently. Rich-result eligibility cannot be inferred from valid JSON alone.
solution: Enrich one consistent business entity with confirmed contact, address, social profiles and appropriate business type. Add accurate Product data where applicable; include Offer only when real price/availability supports it. Validate with Google's rich-result tooling and align shipping/returns markup only after policies are complete.
acceptance: Schema matches visible, approved facts; no fabricated prices/reviews/offers; validators pass relevant checks without guaranteeing rich-result display.

issue: The homepage repeats assurances and delays specific visitor decisions
evidence: The homepage repeats one-partner/experience/quality/speed messages across several sections, adds a service ticker, industry flip cards, a shop grid and a full contact form. Its desktop document height was 10,219 px and the 390 px mobile snapshot 17,155 px. The solutions page presents the general process before the sector details.
why: Length alone is not a defect, but repeated assurances compete with service choice and proof. Mobile visitors must scan a long sequence to find the information relevant to them.
solution: Lead with explicit HVAC service scope and a quote/call action; follow with service pathways, proof, relevant sectors, concise process and contact. Consolidate repeated benefits. On solutions, add an immediate sector index before the general process. Retain useful depth in contextual detail pages.
acceptance: A first-time user can explain the offer, choose a relevant path and locate proof/contact without reading repeated sections; verify through observed usability sessions.

issue: Local contact and credibility information is present but incomplete for decision-making
evidence: Contact clearly separates the Budapest registered address and Szentendre warehouse/correspondence address, and provides phone/email. Impresszum includes tax and registration data. Contact does not state visiting hours, appointment expectations or whether the warehouse accepts customer visits.
why: Prospects need to distinguish legal headquarters from a service/collection location. Search listings should not imply a staffed walk-in venue without business confirmation.
solution: Confirm and publish hours, appointment/collection rules, service area and appropriate directions. Keep name/address/phone consistent across the website and verified listings; review Google Business Profile separately with owner access. Add named technical contacts or accountable expert profiles where appropriate.
acceptance: Each address has a clear role and approved visitor information; external listings are reconciled using authorized access.

issue: Shared assets and render-blocking requests warrant optimization after imagery
evidence: The desktop sample recorded 21 render-blocking resource entries, 20 script-initiated requests and about 330 kB decoded script bodies with visible size data. Homepage HTML is 286,100 decoded bytes. Styles are minified and sampled assets are gzipped with long cache lifetimes; HTML sends no-store.
why: Plugin/template assets can add work on pages where features are not used. Presence does not prove unused code or justify indiscriminate removal.
solution: Profile CSS/JS coverage and long tasks by template; conditionally enqueue shop/form assets, defer only compatible scripts and remove redundant styles after dependency tests. Assess anonymous HTML caching separately from cart/account/checkout. Keep local WOFF2 fonts and review font-display/weight use in a controlled trace.
acceptance: Coverage and repeatable lab traces justify removals; cart, forms, consent and navigation still work; personalized pages are not cached publicly.

issue: Inconsistent and partly untranslated wording weakens polish
evidence: About mixes 20 éve, Közel 20 év and Több mint 20 év while references say 21 év; it also says the company was founded at the end of 2005. Product pages show Contact us now; the shop filter uses Price:; category titles use Archives. Broad warranty/quick-response claims are not qualified with specific terms.
why: Inconsistent dates and template language make a recently updated site look unfinished. Strong promises should match an operationally deliverable commitment.
solution: Prefer stable 2005 óta wording, translate customer-facing defaults and simplify technical jargon without losing accuracy. Publish approved warranty scope and response expectations, not invented guarantees. Have a Hungarian HVAC specialist review nomenclature and customer-facing explanations.
acceptance: No unexplained English UI remains in primary journeys; tenure and guarantees are consistent and fact-checked.

issue: The HTTP www variant has an avoidable redirect hop
evidence: The tested route redirects 301 to https://www.nextro.hu/ and then 301 to https://nextro.hu/. Other tested host/protocol variants resolve correctly.
why: This adds a small delay for visitors and crawlers using the old host/protocol; it is not an indexation emergency.
solution: Where hosting rules permit, combine host and scheme normalization into one permanent redirect directly to the preferred HTTPS non-www URL, preserving path/query and avoiding loops.
acceptance: Every supported legacy host/scheme test reaches the preferred canonical host in one hop; paths and queries remain correct.

issue: Social preview and secondary metadata need finishing
evidence: Open Graph and Twitter-card metadata exist, but shop, contact and category pages lack og:image. Favicon links are present; declared 32/192 px sizes point to filenames containing 150/300, so actual dimensions should be checked before altering them.
why: Commercial links can be less recognizable in messaging/social previews. This is presentation polish, not a demonstrated search-ranking issue.
solution: Add a purposeful branded fallback preview image and category-specific images where useful; validate rendered previews. Verify icon dimensions and browser appearance rather than inferring a failure from filenames.
acceptance: Key pages generate intentional previews; favicon metadata agrees with actual assets or is corrected where necessary.

issue: Anonymous overlay links and color-only inline links need semantic repairs
evidence: axe found an unnamed focusable .gspb-containerlink on services and inline links distinguished only by color on services/contact. The site otherwise exposes a working skip link, associated form labels and visible focus on tested carousel controls.
why: A screen-reader user can land on a link with no purpose; color-dependent links are harder to identify. These are more specific than a blanket claim that keyboard access is broken.
solution: Remove redundant overlay anchors or give the intended link a meaningful accessible name; use real text links and underlines where links occur within prose. Test tab order and avoid nested interactive elements when making cards clickable.
acceptance: No unnamed links in affected templates; links are identifiable without color alone; screen-reader and keyboard spot checks agree with automated results.

issue: Conversion measurement and end-to-end reliability are not yet evidenced
evidence: Public inspection verified routes, labels, empty-cart behavior and UI states but intentionally did not send enquiries, subscribe, create an account or place an order. Analytics, CRM, mail delivery and revenue data were not provided.
why: A visually improved funnel may still lose leads after submission. Without a baseline, no uplift or conversion-rate claim is defensible.
solution: With owner approval use staging/test mode to verify form validation, delivery, spam handling, success feedback, product/cart totals, shipping, payment failure and confirmation. Implement consent-aware quote/call/email/add-to-cart/checkout events and review lead quality as well as volume.
acceptance: Authorized test evidence proves end-to-end delivery and transaction states; events are documented, privacy-reviewed and deduplicated; a baseline is established before optimization experiments.
